questions.text: When INJECT_FAULT is set, at which RAM address does the test see a wrong value each pass (fixed address, or one that changes per pass), and which element and read does it affect? The value in MARCH_FIRST_ERR depends on this.
questions.answer: The address is fixed at 5, with one wrong word seen per pass, and on the first pass MARCH_FIRST_ERR is set to 5. The specification does not say which March element or which read the fault affects. It only says the fault is injected in the checker's compare and never in the stored data.
questions.evidence: INJECT_FAULT makes the test see one wrong word per pass at address 5; that error counts in MARCH_ERRS and, on the first pass, sets MARCH_FIRST_ERR to 5. The fault is injected only in the checker's compare, never in the stored data, so the RAM ends all zero as March C- leaves it.

questions.text: Does one pass run March C- once with the all-zero background and once with the all-one background, or does it alternate backgrounds from pass to pass? What order is used, given that RAM must read all zeros after the last pass?
questions.answer: Every pass runs March C- twice, first with the all-zero background and then with the all-one background. Backgrounds do not alternate from pass to pass. The specification does not say how the RAM ends up all zeros after the all-one background, so I cannot add anything on that.
questions.evidence: - March C- is: up(w0); up(r0,w1); up(r1,w0); down(r0,w1); down(r1,w0); down(r0), with the all-zero background and then the all-one background as the data.  One pass is both backgrounds.

questions.text: What value is read (decimal)? (Scenario: Straight after configuration and reset release, with no writes, MEM_ADDR is set to 5 and RAM_DATA is read once with AUTOINC=0.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: 3235774469 (0xC0DE0005). RAM word 5 holds 0xC0DE0000 + 5 straight after configuration, and a RAM_DATA read with AUTOINC=0 does not change MEM_ADDR.
questions.evidence: - A RAM of 1,024 words of 32 bits. Its power-up contents must be defined: word *i* holds 0xC0DE0000 + *i* straight after configuration, before anyone writes to it.

questions.text: What value does h_rdata show? (Scenario: h_we and h_re asserted in the same clock to SCRATCH (old 0x1, writing 0x2).) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?

After reset, what does MARCH_STATUS bit 0 read and do the bits 31:16 retain 37? (Scenario: A 200-pass march test is running with 37 passes completed when reset is asserted for 8 clocks and released.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: After reset MARCH_STATUS reads 0, so BUSY (bit 0) is 0 and passes completed (bits 31:16) is 0. The count of 37 is not retained.
questions.evidence: Reset: MEM_ADDR 0, MEM_CTRL 0 (AUTOINC off), MARCH_CTRL 0, MARCH_PASSES 1, MARCH_STATUS 0, MARCH_ERRS 0, MARCH_FIRST_ERR 0xFFFFFFFF.

questions.text: How many passes complete and does MARCH_STATUS bit 1 become 1? (Scenario: MARCH_PASSES is 0 and MARCH_CTRL bit 0 is written 1.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: One pass completes, because a MARCH_PASSES value of 0 is treated as 1. The register still reads back 0. MARCH_STATUS bit 1 (DONE) rises when that last pass finishes, and BUSY falls in the same clock.
questions.evidence: - MARCH_PASSES of 0 is treated as 1; the register keeps the value written (the pass count used is max(1, value)). Values above 65,535 cannot be written (16 bits).

questions.text: Does the test restart with counters cleared? (Scenario: MARCH_CTRL bit 0 is written 1 again while a march test is already running at pass 5.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: No. START while BUSY is ignored, so the running test continues and its counters are not cleared.

questions.text: What are MARCH_ERRS (decimal) and the value of MARCH_FIRST_ERR? (Scenario: A 3-pass run with INJECT_FAULT=1 completes; the fault word is at address 0x2A.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: MARCH_ERRS = 3 (one wrong word per pass, 3 passes) and MARCH_FIRST_ERR = 5 (0x00000005). The fault address is fixed at 5 by the specification, so the 0x2A in the scenario does not apply.
questions.evidence: INJECT_FAULT makes the test see one wrong word per pass at address 5; that error counts in MARCH_ERRS and, on the first pass, sets MARCH_FIRST_ERR to 5.

questions.text: What value do MARCH_STATUS bits 31:16 show? (Scenario: A 70000-pass run is requested (MARCH_PASSES exceeds 16 bits) and completes.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: This scenario cannot occur. MARCH_PASSES is 16 bits, so a value above 65,535 cannot be written and a 70,000-pass run cannot be requested. Passes completed in MARCH_STATUS bits 31:16 therefore never has to represent more than 65,535.
questions.evidence: Values above 65,535 cannot be written (16 bits).

questions.topic: Names, files and the build target
questions.answer: The top-level module is `p2_bram_rom_top` in `rtl/p2_bram_rom_top.sv`. The module exposing the h_* register port is the separate core, `p2_bram_rom_core` in `rtl/p2_bram_rom_core.sv`. It has ports clk, rst (active high), h_we, h_re, h_addr[11:0], h_wdata[31:0], h_rdata[31:0] and the design's own signals. The bench drives the core.
questions.evidence: - Names and files: the top-level module is named `p2_bram_rom_top` in `rtl/p2_bram_rom_top.sv`; the register-port core (the logic behind the `h_*` port, with no vendor primitive) is a separate module named `p2_bram_rom_core` in `rtl/p2_bram_rom_core.sv`, with ports `clk`, `rst` (active high), `h_we`, `h_re`, `h_addr[11:0]`, `h_wdata[31:0]`, `h_rdata[31:0]` and the design's own signals. Files are SystemVerilog (`.sv`). The bench drives the core.
